clue.text: Clumsily put together in stone

definitions.meaning: to make or mend it roughly and hastily
a rounded paving stone of the kind used for old streets

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a botched, makeshift assembly job, and a small rounded rock set into a road surface.

clue.text: Intimate missing student is unable to function

indicators.note: missing tells us a piece is dropped from the word for intimate

parts.note: intimate friends are close
L is the learner driver's plate, so a student
is unable means can't, written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A shy pupil cannot cope without a close friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'function' is the definition in its mathematical sense, not a social gathering; CLOSE loses its L to give COSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The cosecant is a trigonometric ratio, one of the standard mathematical functions alongside sine and cosine.

clue.text: It's set to cause damage arising from, for instance, Labour gaffe

parts.note: a boob is a blunder or gaffe

indicators.note: in a down clue, arising means the word reads upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: Labour is an example of a political party

explanation.surface: A political blunder by Labour is a trap set to cause harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arising' reads the party upwards, as a down clue allows, so the political word turns into YTRAP after the blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden device rigged to go off when disturbed is laid in wait to harm its victim.

clue.text: Wail of useless conservationists

parts.note: a lame excuse is a feeble, useless one
NT is the National Trust, a British heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: A complaint about ineffective environmental campaigners.
explanation.walkthrough: NT, the National Trust, is a British charity that conserves historic houses and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A lament is a cry of grief, an expression of mourning like a wail.

clue.text: Archaism involved with god-given power

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of archaism are jumbled

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned expression linked with divine authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' scrambles ARCHAISM.
explanation.definitionFit: In its original theological sense, charisma is a divinely conferred gift or grace.

clue.text: Butler?

parts.note: a surname taken from a job done in a domestic establishment, such as Cook, Butler or Steward

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Butler' as a famous person and it hints at someone everyone knows; read it as a title from domestic service and it is literally the name of a household role.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a famous name, and Butler is also the name of a post within a domestic staff.

clue.text: Waste problem is filling empty bath

parts.note: a rub is a difficulty, as in 'there's the rub'

indicators.note: filling means one piece goes inside the shell of another
empty means the word bath loses its middle, keeping its outer letters

explanation.surface: A drainage trouble with a bathtub that has been drained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves only the first and last letters of bath; 'filling' puts the word is inside those two.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbish is refuse, material thrown away as useless.

clue.text: Slight conclusion of insufferable goo

parts.note: slight and slim both mean slender or small

indicators.note: conclusion of points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A minor end to something unbearable and sticky.
explanation.definitionFit: Slime is a viscous, slippery substance, exactly the kind of thing called goo.

clue.text: Open-frame construction's not for early humanoids

indicators.note: construction says the letters are rebuilt, and not says some letters are left out of the build

explanation.surface: An open-frame building is unsuitable for primitive people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'construction's not for' tells you to rearrange OPENFRAME after taking out F, O and R, leaving PENAME to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Ape-men is an old name for primitive hominids thought to bridge apes and humans.

clue.text: Suddenly attack high hill held by officer

indicators.note: held by means one piece is grasped inside the other

parts.note: SM is a sergeant major
a tor is a rocky hilltop, common on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A soldier commanded to charge a fortified hilltop.
explanation.walkthrough: A TOR is a rocky hill in south-west England; SM (sergeant major) holds it.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm a position is to assault and capture it in a sudden rush.

clue.text: Suspender showing right up

parts.note: a hanging weighted cord that reveals whether a wall stands truly vertical

explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspender' suggests underwear; it is anything that hangs, and 'right up' means exactly vertical.
explanation.definitionFit: A builder's weighted string hangs straight down to show true vertical.

clue.text: Spender's allowance?

parts.note: Stephen Spender was an English poet, so his allowance is the freedom granted to writers of verse

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spender' looks like a big spender with pocket money; it is the poet Stephen Spender.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a writer's freedom to bend grammar or fact for effect, a liberty allowed to versifiers.

clue.text: Spicy stuff read out from two letters

indicators.note: read out means the letters are spoken, and their names make the sound we want

parts.note: the letter K and the letter N, said as their names

explanation.surface: Someone reading spice names from a pair of characters.
explanation.walkthrough: Say the letter names K and N one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Cayenne is a hot red pepper powder used to season food.

clue.text: Said I am over whammy

indicators.note: over means the whole run is turned round
said means a word spoken, so the letter is replaced by a word sounding like it

parts.note: the pronoun, which sounds like the organ of sight
I am means I exist, I live

explanation.surface: Someone declaring they are finished with a run of bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Said' turns the pronoun into the organ of sight by sound; 'am' stands for 'I live', I exist; 'over' turns the whole run back to front, giving EVILEYE from EYELIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A whammy is a jinx or curse, the malevolent look supposedly cast by a witch.

clue.text: Annoy singer

definitions.meaning: someone who sings to the police, a police informer

explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses the word both as a verb meaning irritate and as a noun for a police informer, who sings to detectives.

clue.text: Glance at departing theocratic assembly

indicators.note: assembly means putting the remaining letters together in a new order

explanation.surface: A look at a religious council leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at departing' takes A and T out of THEOCRATIC; 'assembly' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: To glance off is to rebound at an angle, which is what a ricochet does.

clue.text: Partner is about to become known

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spouse is about to be revealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is about' looks like 'is going to', but 'is' is fodder and 'about' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Transpire, in its looser sense, means to come to light or emerge as fact.

clue.text: With only one bishop, church's an institution in temporary disuse

indicators.note: with only one says a doubled letter is cut down to a single instance

parts.note: an abbey is a monastic institution
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church with just one bishop left has an institution that has fallen out of use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With only one' cuts the doubled bishop letter in the monastic building down to one, giving ABEY; 'in' is a link to the definition, and CE is the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of abeyance is suspension, when a right or practice is set aside for a time.

clue.text: Prig's occupied by city with large bar

indicators.note: occupied by means the other pieces sit inside this one

parts.note: a prude is a prig
EC is the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: A prim person takes over a large city bar.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the London postcode area for the financial district, the City.
explanation.definitionFit: To preclude something is to rule it out, to bar it from happening.

clue.text: Lug in that case of clay

parts.note: lug is informal British for ear
then means in that case, as in 'then do it'

explanation.surface: Carry a clay pot in that event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lug' looks like a verb meaning haul; it is British slang for an ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthen means made of baked earth, as clay pottery is.

clue.text: Wedge book in side of opening

parts.note: to wedge something is to jam it

explanation.surface: Push a book against the doorframe to prop it open.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamb is the vertical post forming each side of a door or window frame.

clue.text: As Lady Macbeth wanted to do to tyrant?

definitions.text: As Lady Macbeth wanted to do
definitions.meaning: Lady Macbeth cries 'Out, damned spot!', wishing to clear her hand of a stain
an absolute ruler who wields power cruelly

explanation.definitionFit: Read as de-spot it means remove a stain, Lady Macbeth's wish; as one word it means an oppressive autocrat.

clue.text: Instinctive as old city is to nature

parts.words: as old city is to nature
parts.note: Ur, the ancient Sumerian city, sits inside the word nature; the answer states where it sits, split as a phrase, with Ur taken away

explanation.surface: Something natural compared to an ancient city's link with the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: A riddle rather than a mechanism: say where the old city of Ur lies within the word nature, then remove the city, and the phrase closes up into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Innate qualities are inborn, present by nature rather than learned.

clue.text: One learning from experience of one following prime suspect about

indicators.note: following places the single letter after the jumbled piece
suspect here means dubious, so the letters of prime are unreliable and rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
C is circa, about

explanation.surface: A learner shadowing a leading suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges the five letters of prime into EMPIR; 'following' puts the Roman one after it, then circa's C.
explanation.definitionFit: An empiric is someone who relies on observation and practice rather than theory.

clue.text: Father covers chest with warm jacket

indicators.note: covers means one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
an ark is a chest or box, as in the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: Dad wraps his chest in a cosy coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A parka is a hooded insulated coat for cold weather.

clue.text: Pardon Johnson being out refuge

indicators.note: being out means this name lies on the outside of the other piece

parts.note: Amy Johnson was a pioneering English aviator
a nest is a snug refuge

explanation.surface: Excuse a Johnson for leaving a shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: Amy Johnson was the English pilot who flew solo to Australia in 1930.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesty is a general pardon, usually granted by a government.

clue.text: Maybe fish with split cane

parts.note: the perch is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: split means broken apart, so the letters of cane are reshuffled

explanation.surface: An angler might land something with a cracked rod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'split' rearranges the fishing rod's letters into ANCE, the end of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Perchance is an old-fashioned word for perhaps.

clue.text: Malignant houses make a row

indicators.note: houses means the word contains the letters we want inside it

explanation.surface: A harmful growth sets out in a line.
explanation.definitionFit: To align things is to place them in a straight line.

clue.text: Nitrates involved in hobby kit?

indicators.note: involved means mixed together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Chemical compounds used in a craft set.
explanation.definitionFit: A model railway set is equipment for a pastime, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Rigorous as always between points

indicators.note: between places one piece inside the two points

parts.note: S and E are compass points
ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: Being strict as usual in a debate.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe means harsh or strict, like a rigorous regime.
